title: Grieving mom demands Taser answers
article: A grieving mom is demanding to know why Vancouver police shot her son with a Taser.
Roman Andreichikov was high on crack cocaine in his Granville Street apartment when Const. Darren Hall shot him twice with a Taser.
Within minutes, the 25-year-old died from cardiac arrest. Now, a coroner's inquest is investigating the death of May 1, 2004.

"I am hoping somebody will be responsible for using this Taser gun," Diana Andreichikov, flanked by Roman's dad, Oleg, and his younger brother, Pavel, 17, said yesterday. "I don't believe he needed this much force. He wasn't dangerous to nobody."
The personal trainer had been on a five-day drug binge when his friend called 911 for an ambulance.
Instead, five constables, including Hall, arrived, along with a supervising sergeant.
Vancouver Det. Catherine Cheryl Rogers testified that Andreichikov could have been in a state of "excited delirium," a state of superhuman strength brought on by heavy cocaine use.
Police struggled with Andreichikov as they restrained him, shooting him twice with the Taser.
"I really don't know in this case whether anything could have been done differently with the training and device," said Rogers.
Girlfriend Jamie Leno testified Andreichikov was not violent earlier. She said he was paranoid and verbally abusive, accusing her of being unfaithful, which she denied.
Hall's Taser was fired 43 times between April 20 and May 1, including seven times in one day.

"I believe eventually Tasers will be shown to be a cause of heart attacks in people with cocaine psychosis, but I don't believe we have the science at the moment," said Phil Rankin, the lawyer for the Andreichikov family.
Police say Tasers, which fire 50,000-volt shocks in five-second bursts, safely immobilize suspects.
Police lawyers are expected to argue that Andreichikov died from the effects of cocaine, not the Taser. There have been five Taser deaths in B.C.
